results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004952 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. According to the Virtual Fly Brain database, the mushroom body is divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle, and the mushroom body lobe system, consisting of a vertical and a medial branch. Virtual Fly Brain holds extensive data on the mushroom body, including neurons, parts, and images, with, for example, [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004952,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons having some part in the mushroom body and [22137](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004952,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in mushroom body") images of such neurons.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: According to the VFB database, there are several types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain, including alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells. The gamma Kenyon cells are further subdivided into subtypes. As documented in VFB, these subtypes are based on the lobes they project their axons to, such as the gamma lobe, the alpha and beta lobes, and the alpha' and beta' lobes, as described by Lee et al., 1999, and Aso et al., 2014. VFB holds specific data on gamma Kenyon cells, including images, subclasses, expression patterns, scRNAseq data, and transgene expression.

results.title: Basic connectivity
results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons, as stated in the VFB database. According to the VFB database, these neurons feed reward or punishment information into the mushroom body. VFB holds extensive data on adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons, including [2415](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") images, [21](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") subclasses, scRNAseq data from [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,anatScRNAseqQuery "Run in VFB: scRNAseq data for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") sources, transgene expression data from [64](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") sources, downstream connectivity classes for [316](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") neurons, and upstream connectivity classes for [1290](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") neurons.

results.title: Gene expression
results.question: What neurotransmitter do mushroom body Kenyon cells use?
results.response: The primary neurotransmitter used by [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") Kenyon cells is acetylcholine. This information comes from the VFB database, which supports [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") as cholinergic, i.e. using acetylcholine, based on VFB neurotransmitter tags. Additionally, VFB holds extensive data related to the mushroom body, including neurons with some part in the mushroom body, synaptic terminals, presynaptic and postsynaptic terminals, parts of the mushroom body, subclasses, tracts/nerves innervating it, lineage clones, images of neurons, and expression patterns overlapping the mushroom body.

results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to the mushroom body and lateral horn. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database, which states that the antennal lobe sends synaptic output to the mushroom body and that antennal lobe projection neurons have axons that project to higher brain centers, including the mushroom body calyx and/or lateral horn.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila central brain contains approximately more than 125,000 neurons, according to the VFB database, as retrieved from VFB. VFB also holds data on the [adult central brain astrocyte-like glial cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047885 "Open adult central brain astrocyte-like glial cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), including [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047885,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of adult central brain astrocyte-like glial cell") subclasses and [3](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047885,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in adult central brain astrocyte-like glial cell") instances of transgene expression.

results.response:
The main components of the [adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004913 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain") include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the three paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge, as stated in the VFB database. The adult central complex is associated with various functions, although specific functions of its components are not detailed in the provided evidence. 

VFB holds a range of data related to the adult central complex, including images, neuron information, parts of the complex, and transgene expression data. results.title: Circuit motif
results.question: Describe the dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs). Which DAN types connect to which MBON types?
results.response:
The dopaminergic input to [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") output neurons (MBONs) comes from various types of dopaminergic neurons. According to the Virtual Fly Brain database, there are 77 upstream class-connectivity partners matching "dopaminergic neuron" for MBON, including adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons and mushroom body PPL1 neurons. Specifically, dopaminergic input to MBONs comes from specific types of dopaminergic neurons, including PPL1 and PAM neurons, as well as mushroom body dopaminergic neurons and adult dopaminergic neurons. 

VFB holds data on neurons with some part in mushroom body, including [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in mushroom body, [599](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body, and [367](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body. Additionally, VFB has information on [22137](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in mushroom body") images of neurons with some part in mushroom body and [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,ExpressionOverlapsHere "Run in VFB: Expression patterns overlapping mushroom body") expression patterns overlapping mushroom body. 

The specific connection between DAN types and MBON types is not fully detailed in the provided information, but the Virtual Fly Brain database contains connectivity data, including 13460 pairwise connections and 36 connected neurons out of 37 total neurons.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") visual neuron type has an ID of [1813403998](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open 1813403998 in Virtual Fly Brain"). It is a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron, with a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer. The dendritic arbor extends outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer. LPLC2 is involved in detecting looming stimuli and is thought to elicit a jump escape response. In terms of connections, LPLC2 is linked to various neurons, including adult cholinergic neurons, T5c neurons, and transmedullary neurons. This information is based on data from the VFB database, which summarizes neuron profiles and provides term information, as well as research by Wu et al. (2016) and Klapoetke et al. (2017).

results.title: Pathway tracing
results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?
results.response:
To trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn, we can consider the intermediate neuron types and their connections. According to the literature, a high-level pathway is supported by VFB, which involves the following steps: olfactory receptor neurons (ORN) -> antennal lobe projection neuron -> lateral horn. 

In this pathway, antennal lobe projection neurons act as intermediate neurons, connecting the olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. The [adult lateral horn](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn in Virtual Fly Brain") is the target region, and it receives synaptic inputs from these projection neurons.

VFB holds a significant amount of data related to the adult lateral horn, including images, neurons with specific parts or terminals in this region, tracts/nerves innervating it, lineage clones, and transgene expression data. For instance, there are [1661](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult lateral horn") neurons with some part in the adult lateral horn, and [1658](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in adult lateral horn") neurons with synaptic terminals in this region. Additionally, VFB has information on [64](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,LineageClonesIn "Run in VFB: Lineage clones found in adult lateral horn") lineage clones found in the adult lateral horn and [1935](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in adult lateral horn") instances of transgene expression in this region.

Regarding the specific types of neurons in the lateral horn, such as the [adult lateral horn Leucokinin neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn Leucokinin neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), VFB does not provide direct information on their connections to olfactory receptor neurons in the given evidence. However, the available data on neurons and their terminals in the adult lateral horn can be used to further investigate the neural circuits involving these neurons. 

In summary, the pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn involves antennal lobe projection neurons as intermediate neurons, and VFB provides a wealth of information on the adult lateral horn, including neuronal anatomy and gene expression.

results.title: Anatomical containment chain
results.question: Trace the anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure. What is each level in the hierarchy?
results.response:
The anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure is as follows: 
DA1 glomerulus -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain. 
This information comes from the VFB database, which provides the anatomical containment hierarchy for the DA1 glomerulus. 
VFB also holds data on neurons and images related to the DA1 glomerulus, including neurons with some part in [antennal lobe glomerulus DA1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003932 "Open antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 in Virtual Fly Brain"), neurons with synaptic terminals in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, and images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), specifically the [DNp01](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open DNp01 in Virtual Fly Brain"), is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as described by Thomas and Wyman (1984). Its distinct anatomy includes a large descending axon, which is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective, and it arborizes in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, as noted in the literature (Power, 1948; Koto et al., 1981). 

VFB holds extensive data on the DNp01, including [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images, [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression, [361](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") downstream connectivity classes, and [435](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") upstream connectivity classes. This wealth of information can be used to further understand the anatomy, connectivity, and function of the giant fiber neuron. 

For example, the expression pattern of the P{VT046265-GAL4} driver line in DNp01 is available, providing a tool for further study of this neuron. 

Relevant publications, such as those by Thomas and Wyman (1984), Power (1948), and Koto et al. (1981), offer insights into the giant fiber neuron's role in jump escape behavior and its unique anatomical features. 

Overall, the giant fiber neuron, or DNp01, is a well-studied neuron with a distinct profile of anatomy, connectivity, and available driver lines, making it an important subject for continued research in Drosophila neuroscience.
